A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and support a complete comparison of text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. The appendices match in text and rendered content apart from page-number footers.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments evaluating gender bias across 11 QE metrics, three datasets, and eight target languages, together with downstream filtering and decoding analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical evaluations and their main-text and appendix results.

M1.justification: The contrastive evaluation framework, QE models, context-concatenation strategies, GEMBA prompts, and quality-aware decoding procedure are unchanged. The added mitigation ideas are future work, not implemented method components.

E1.justification: Both versions use MT-GenEval, GATE, and mGeNTE with identical language and scenario coverage. Gender ambiguity, contextual disambiguation, neutral translations, automatic translation assessment, and downstream decoding tasks are retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated neural and GEMBA metric sets and experiment-specific comparisons are unchanged. Newly named CLIPScore, BERTScore, MoverScore, and BLEURT appear in related work, not as additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Data subsets, evaluation metrics, Google Translate filtering, and decoding settings are unchanged. Section 5.3 still reranks 50 hypotheses generated with epsilon sampling at 0.02; Appendix A retains the same experimental procedures.

E4.justification: The bias-versus-brittleness analysis in Section 4.3, prompt-variant comparisons, context-translator comparison in Figure 9, tie analysis in Table 14, and filtering case study remain unchanged. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same 95% confidence intervals, paired bootstrap tests and one-sample t-tests in Appendix A.2, and Wilcoxon tests in Appendix A.3. Run, seed, and uncertainty-reporting information is unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted findings, and significance highlighting are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 4 retains delta-M values of -45.67 for greedy decoding, -46.84 for QAD with CometKiwi 22, and -43.47 for QAD with CometKiwi 23 XXL.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2), QE score ratios, error and tie definitions, score rescaling, and parity criteria are unchanged. No mathematical reasoning, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about gender bias in QE, disadvantages for feminine and neutral translations, and downstream effects on filtering and decoding. Abstract edits do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The Limitations section adds interpretability-driven selection of few-shot examples as a possible remedy for bias introduced by context translation, alongside the previously mentioned fine-tuning. This makes the future mitigation discussion more specific without changing existing findings or applicability limits.

D1.justification: Footnote 1 changes the advertised code and artifact repository from g8a9/gender-bias-qe-metrics to deep-spin/gender-bias-qe-metrics. Appendix A's implementation details, checkpoint identifiers, prompts, filtering instructions, and hardware disclosure are unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 2.2 substantially expands coverage of gender-bias measurement and mitigation in MT and explicitly distinguishes this literature from the paper's QE focus. Section 2.3 adds specific NLG-metric precedents, and the limitations discussion gains relevant references. These additions extend research positioning beyond the accompanying bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized abstract and prose edits, organizes related work into three numbered subsections, renames Section 4.1 from Gender-Ambiguous Entities to Gender-Ambiguous Instances, and adds an equal-contribution footnote and acknowledgements. The broader scientific narrative and appendix organization remain stable.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables retain their designs and content, but their placement changes locally: Table 2 moves from PDF page 5 to page 6, while Figure 4 and Table 3 are rearranged on page 7. v4 also omits printed page-number footers and lightly edits Table 4's caption.

improvement.justification: New Section 2.2 addresses v3's limited discussion of directly relevant gender-bias measurement and mitigation research, making the contribution easier to situate. Local editorial improvements and a more specific future-work discussion provide a limited quality gain; the scientific evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
